bull_bear.body:
- Established brand presence in Gurugram's Sushant Lok micro-market, with Club Florence described as an already branded name in the hospitality sector and Boom Plaza running with established outlets and branded shops
- Rent-yielding and annuity assets (Boom Plaza commercial complex, Club Florence and Ansal Riverdale clubs) alongside the development business
- Large land-bank style township footprint across multiple states - about 150 acres at Florence Town Jaipur, about 80 acres at Ansal Basera City Jhansi, about 64 acres at Ansal City Amritsar and about 16 acres at Florence Estate Amritsar
- Florence Triangle site has come under the TOD policy with FAR increased from 1.5 to 3.5, raising the development potential of an already-held site
- Internal control framework reviewed by independent internal auditors (M/s Shailender K. Bajaj & Co.) with four Audit Committee meetings during the year
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Price risk through the real-estate price cycle — Management calls this the big risk developers face: real estate price cycles have the maximum impact on developer margins because land costs account for a large portion of the constructed property. For a plotted-township developer holding land at Jaipur, Jhansi, Amritsar and Pathankot, a down-cycle compresses margin on inventory already carried at cost.
- Demand risk - the ability to sell completed product — Flagged explicitly in Risk and Concerns as the ability to sell properties based on location, brand, track record, quality and timelines of completion, addressed only by market surveys. The portfolio's dependence on unsold plot inventory (Kochi balance plots, Amritsar, Jaipur) makes absorption the primary revenue lever; Opportunities and Threats adds that fluctuations in market conditions may affect the ability to sell projects at expected prices, which could adversely affect revenue and earnings.
- Finance risk and funding availability, with interest-rate uncertainty — Management states there is Finance Risk also and that low availability of funds is a major risk for the real estate industry, and that uncertain interest rates lead to uncertainty in the real estate market. Finance cost is a standing charge on a long-gestation plotted-development model where cash comes in only on sale.
- Land supply constraints — Stated twice in Opportunities and Threats: potential limitations on the supply of land could reduce the Company's revenues or negatively impact the results of its operations. The business can only be sustained by replenishing developable land.
- Regulatory, approval and sanctioning delay risk — The business is subject to extensive statutory or governmental regulations; the sanctioning process through the authorities is slow and time consuming; and change in government business policies or tax structure may affect prospects. Management also flags the lack of uniformity in the regulatory environment concerning real estate as a concern for attracting FDI. The project review shows this biting in practice - RERA renewal awaited at Jhansi, RERA registration still being applied for at Kochi's Area Beyond Thodu, completion certificates applied for or only partly received, and revenue/municipal data-bank changes holding up plot sales in Kerala.
- Litigation and insolvency exposure on specific projects — The SADA, Gwalior (MP) group-housing project allotted through competitive bidding is sub judice after SADA's cancellation order and awaits final hearing; 'Ansal Crown Heights', the Sector-80 Faridabad project taken over from the Crown Group JV, is under NCLT proceedings following legal issues filed by clients; and one wholly owned subsidiary is under CIRP. Each is capital locked in a project that cannot currently be monetised.
- Planning-policy dependence stalling held assets — Construction of the Florence Triangle commercial complex in Sushant Lok-II, Gurugram has not progressed during this year as well because the site came under TOD policy; the FAR rose from 1.5 to 3.5 and the Company is still working out how best to utilise it. A favourable policy change has nonetheless frozen a developable commercial site for a second consecutive year.
- Labour availability and work stoppages — Opportunities and Threats states work stoppages and other labour problems could adversely affect the business, and Risk and Concerns adds the availability of quality manpower as an industry concern. Construction progress at Jhansi, Pathankot, Jaipur and the Kochi club building depends on continuous site labour.
- Board-level view that no existential risk exists beyond global market volatility — The Directors' Report Risk Management Policy section states that during the year under review, no element of risk except volatile market condition all over the world and its after effect has been identified which in the opinion of the Board may threaten the existence of the Company in the long run. That is a narrow articulation for a company with two projects in litigation or NCLT and a subsidiary under CIRP, and is itself a governance watch-item.

business.body: Ansal Buildwell develops and sells residential plots, independent floors, villas and group-housing flats, and develops and operates commercial complexes and recreational clubs. Its projects span Gurugram (Boom Plaza commercial complex, Club Florence, Florence Triangle, Premium Floors), Kochi (Ansal City / Florence Heights, City Homes, Ansal Riverdale club), Amritsar and Pathankot in Punjab, Jaipur in Rajasthan and Jhansi in UP. Development is carried out both directly and through wholly owned subsidiaries and joint-venture companies such as Ansal JKD Pearl Developers.

- **Commercial:** Boom Plaza (Sushant Lok-III, Sector-57, Gurugram), Florence Triangle (F Block, Sushant Lok-II, Gurugram)

outlook.body:
- Work out how best to utilise the additional FAR at the Florence Triangle commercial site in Sushant Lok-II, Gurugram, which has come under the TOD policy with FAR raised from 1.5 to 3.5 - construction has not progressed for a second year pending that decision
- Convert held township land into plotted product: develop the Area Beyond Thodu at Ansal City Kochi as a plotted colony once RERA registration comes through, and commence development of the about 16-acre Florence Estate plotted township in Amritsar
- Monetise the annuity/club estate more intensively - upgrade Ansal Riverdale club (Eroor, Kochi) through a professional vendor and open membership to outside members, with a proposal already sent to the RWA, to lift footfall, revenue and profitability
- Complete and hand over the in-flight township infrastructure - Jhansi electrification, STP and water harvesting, Pathankot services and boundary wall, Jaipur roads, kerbs and parks - and pursue the pending completion certificates and RERA renewals
- Build out the Community Centre at Ansal City, Amritsar, where drawings are approved and construction has started
- Extend beyond the National Capital Region into other cities where demand for residential property, particularly plots, continues to grow
- Adopt green building practices - water harvesting, pollution-control measures and tree plantation - in line with the industry transformation management describes
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Ansal Buildwell's expansion is project development rather than plant capex, and the MD&A project review is the only narrative the bundle carries. In Gurugram, Boom Plaza (Sushant Lok-III, Sector-57) is operating with established outlets; Club Florence (Sector-56) is operating; construction of the Florence Triangle commercial complex in F Block, Sushant Lok-II has not progressed for a second year because the site came under the TOD policy and FAR rose from 1.5 to 3.5, and the Company is working out how best to use the additional FAR; the high-end four-bedroom Premium Floors are complete and possessions are being taken. At Ansal City, Kochi, Florence Heights flats are occupied, City Homes construction is complete and customers have moved in, the Area Beyond Thodu is to be developed as a plotted colony with red earth filling, roads and services to be taken up immediately after RERA registration (application under process), boundary-wall repairs along the Thodu continue, and the club building is under construction with Ground Floor columns and staircase casting in progress and swimming-pool piling complete. At Ansal Riverdale, Eroor (Kochi) the Company proposes to upgrade club facilities through a professional vendor and open membership to outsiders. In Punjab, Ansal City - Amritsar (about 64 acres) is fully developed and re-launched; drawings for its Community Centre are approved, construction has started and the Ground Floor slab was expected to be cast by end-May 2026; Royal Villas construction is complete for some units with completion certificates obtained for eight; Florence Estate, Amritsar (about 16 acres) has a completed site office and sample flat with plotted-township development works expected to commence. At Florence City, Pathankot two sample villas are complete, revised zoning plans are approved, sewerage, electrification, drainage, road and horticulture works are in progress, the bridge over the Khaddi Khad and its approach-road blacktop are complete and almost 40% of the boundary wall is done. At Florence Town, Jaipur (about 150 acres) the revised layout is approved, the substation and electrical scheme have been handed to the discom, roads are laid, kerb-stone work and park boundary walls are in progress, a part completion certificate has been received, and Ansal JKD Pearl Developers has tied up with M/s Sanjeevni Group for plot sales. At Ansal Basera City, Jhansi (about 80 acres) the revised external electrification scheme is approved by UPPCL, about 85% of internal/external electrification and feeder work is complete, water-harvesting construction is in progress, the STP work is to start shortly, environmental clearance is obtained and the project is UP-RERA registered, while RERA renewal and the applied-for completion certificate are awaited. Two projects are stalled in dispute: the SADA Gwalior group-housing allotment is sub judice and Ansal Crown Heights, Sector-80 Faridabad is under NCLT proceedings. The Directors' Report records Nil capital investment on energy conservation and Nil R&D expenditure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained investment momentum in the 2026 Indian real estate market driven by premium residential demand, infrastructure development and moderated interest rates
- Shift toward high-end and luxury housing, with new launches driven by rising income levels and Non Resident Indian participation; premium housing dominated 2025-26 sales and raised market value despite a slight decline in total unit launches
- Demand for luxury properties and integrated townships preferred by end users, with infrastructure development further boosting the market and mid-segment buyers looking for opportunities
- NCR remains one of the most preferred residential destinations, and Gurugram has emerged as a vibrant hub attracting businesses, large corporates and young professionals
- Market composition has moved from pure speculation to a mix of investors and end-users, driven by anticipated job creation, industrial investment and improved connectivity
- The Noida International Airport (Jewar) is transforming the Delhi NCR market, with price appreciation along the Yamuna Expressway and residential property value forecast to rise further by 2027, plus a rise in commercial projects, warehouse hubs and retail space
- Demand across both commercial and residential segments expected to remain healthy, with a greater push for environmental, social and technology-adept built structures guiding long-term strategies
- Structural demand drivers intact - increasing urbanization, favourable demographics, service-sector growth and rising incomes; a demand-supply gap in affordable housing fuelled by tax incentives and a growing middle class with higher savings
- Increasing demand for commercial and office space, especially from the growing Retail, IT and Hospitality sectors
- Outside NCR, demand for residential properties and particularly plots is expected to continue growing, which management expects to contribute to

risks.risk: Price risk through the real-estate price cycle
risks.note: Management calls this the big risk developers face: real estate price cycles have the maximum impact on developer margins because land costs account for a large portion of the constructed property. For a plotted-township developer holding land at Jaipur, Jhansi, Amritsar and Pathankot, a down-cycle compresses margin on inventory already carried at cost.

risks.risk: Demand risk - the ability to sell completed product
risks.note: Flagged explicitly in Risk and Concerns as the ability to sell properties based on location, brand, track record, quality and timelines of completion, addressed only by market surveys. The portfolio's dependence on unsold plot inventory (Kochi balance plots, Amritsar, Jaipur) makes absorption the primary revenue lever; Opportunities and Threats adds that fluctuations in market conditions may affect the ability to sell projects at expected prices, which could adversely affect revenue and earnings.

risks.risk: Finance risk and funding availability, with interest-rate uncertainty
risks.note: Management states there is Finance Risk also and that low availability of funds is a major risk for the real estate industry, and that uncertain interest rates lead to uncertainty in the real estate market. Finance cost is a standing charge on a long-gestation plotted-development model where cash comes in only on sale.

Stated twice in Opportunities and Threats: potential limitations on the supply of land could reduce the Company's revenues or negatively impact the results of its operations. The business can only be sustained by replenishing developable land.

risks.risk: Regulatory, approval and sanctioning delay risk
risks.note: The business is subject to extensive statutory or governmental regulations; the sanctioning process through the authorities is slow and time consuming; and change in government business policies or tax structure may affect prospects. Management also flags the lack of uniformity in the regulatory environment concerning real estate as a concern for attracting FDI. The project review shows this biting in practice - RERA renewal awaited at Jhansi, RERA registration still being applied for at Kochi's Area Beyond Thodu, completion certificates applied for or only partly received, and revenue/municipal data-bank changes holding up plot sales in Kerala.

risks.risk: Litigation and insolvency exposure on specific projects
risks.note: The SADA, Gwalior (MP) group-housing project allotted through competitive bidding is sub judice after SADA's cancellation order and awaits final hearing; 'Ansal Crown Heights', the Sector-80 Faridabad project taken over from the Crown Group JV, is under NCLT proceedings following legal issues filed by clients; and one wholly owned subsidiary is under CIRP. Each is capital locked in a project that cannot currently be monetised.

Construction of the Florence Triangle commercial complex in Sushant Lok-II, Gurugram has not progressed during this year as well because the site came under TOD policy; the FAR rose from 1.5 to 3.5 and the Company is still working out how best to utilise it. A favourable policy change has nonetheless frozen a developable commercial site for a second consecutive year.

Opportunities and Threats states work stoppages and other labour problems could adversely affect the business, and Risk and Concerns adds the availability of quality manpower as an industry concern. Construction progress at Jhansi, Pathankot, Jaipur and the Kochi club building depends on continuous site labour.

risks.risk: Board-level view that no existential risk exists beyond global market volatility
risks.note: The Directors' Report Risk Management Policy section states that during the year under review, no element of risk except volatile market condition all over the world and its after effect has been identified which in the opinion of the Board may threaten the existence of the Company in the long run. That is a narrow articulation for a company with two projects in litigation or NCLT and a subsidiary under CIRP, and is itself a governance watch-item.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained investment momentum in the 2026 Indian real estate market driven by premium residential demand, infrastructure development and moderated interest rates
- Shift toward high-end and luxury housing, with new launches driven by rising income levels and Non Resident Indian participation; premium housing dominated 2025-26 sales and raised market value despite a slight decline in total unit launches
- Demand for luxury properties and integrated townships preferred by end users, with infrastructure development further boosting the market and mid-segment buyers looking for opportunities
- NCR remains one of the most preferred residential destinations, and Gurugram has emerged as a vibrant hub attracting businesses, large corporates and young professionals
- Market composition has moved from pure speculation to a mix of investors and end-users, driven by anticipated job creation, industrial investment and improved connectivity
- The Noida International Airport (Jewar) is transforming the Delhi NCR market, with price appreciation along the Yamuna Expressway and residential property value forecast to rise further by 2027, plus a rise in commercial projects, warehouse hubs and retail space
- Demand across both commercial and residential segments expected to remain healthy, with a greater push for environmental, social and technology-adept built structures guiding long-term strategies
- Structural demand drivers intact - increasing urbanization, favourable demographics, service-sector growth and rising incomes; a demand-supply gap in affordable housing fuelled by tax incentives and a growing middle class with higher savings
- Increasing demand for commercial and office space, especially from the growing Retail, IT and Hospitality sectors
- Outside NCR, demand for residential properties and particularly plots is expected to continue growing, which management expects to contribute to

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Work out how best to utilise the additional FAR at the Florence Triangle commercial site in Sushant Lok-II, Gurugram, which has come under the TOD policy with FAR raised from 1.5 to 3.5 - construction has not progressed for a second year pending that decision
- Convert held township land into plotted product: develop the Area Beyond Thodu at Ansal City Kochi as a plotted colony once RERA registration comes through, and commence development of the about 16-acre Florence Estate plotted township in Amritsar
- Monetise the annuity/club estate more intensively - upgrade Ansal Riverdale club (Eroor, Kochi) through a professional vendor and open membership to outside members, with a proposal already sent to the RWA, to lift footfall, revenue and profitability
- Complete and hand over the in-flight township infrastructure - Jhansi electrification, STP and water harvesting, Pathankot services and boundary wall, Jaipur roads, kerbs and parks - and pursue the pending completion certificates and RERA renewals
- Build out the Community Centre at Ansal City, Amritsar, where drawings are approved and construction has started
- Extend beyond the National Capital Region into other cities where demand for residential property, particularly plots, continues to grow
- Adopt green building practices - water harvesting, pollution-control measures and tree plantation - in line with the industry transformation management describes
